description: How far AI can perform each type of IT work over time, the verification it still needs, and the growth of IT work demand.
How fast each employer adopts AI in its own delivery work, spurred by AI's cost against labour and by competitive pressure.
Client sectors' own AI use, line-of-business staff, applications, seats and IT budgets, and the IT work demand they create.
How each sector's IT backlog is shared among employers, their delivery capacity and productivity, and the work completed or abandoned.
Each employer's staff level mix, the visa policy lever, desired headcount, vacancies and promotions.
Regional unemployment, job switching, visa flows, exits and layoffs, hiring, time to fill, and the seeker and student pools.
How each client sector divides its IT work among in-house teams, its captive GCC and three vendors, from their costs and risks.
Delivered work, wages, labour and AI costs, the vendors' contract books, prices, revenue and margins, and services spend.
